name: Lans
kurzbeschreibung: Exclusive residential and holiday community in the Mittelgebirge with the luxury hotel Schlosshotel Igens and panoramic views.
beschreibung:
Overview

Lans is an elegant and historic alpine village nestled upon the southeastern Mittelgebirge plateau overlooking the Tyrolean provincial capital Innsbruck in the Innsbruck-Land district. Situated at an elevation of 864 metres on a sun-drenched mountain balcony at the foot of Mount Patscherkofel, Lans is home to approximately 1,150 residents. The community seamlessly unites peaceful rural village charm, sophisticated lifestyle, and close proximity to urban amenities. Renowned internationally for picturesque Lake Lans (Lanser See), one of the oldest natural moorland bathing lakes in western Austria, Lans is also celebrated for the protected Lanser Moor nature reserve and a distinguished culinary tradition featuring award-winning heritage inns.

History

Evidence of human habitation on the Lans plateau extends back to the prehistoric Bronze and Iron Ages, substantiated by archaeological findings on the adjacent Lanser Kopf hill and Bergisel. The community first appeared in historical records around 1180 under the name Lannes. For centuries, Lans prospered as an agricultural hamlet along the ancient alpine transit route traversing the Mittelgebirge. The late-Gothic parish church of Saint Lambert, consecrated during the 14th century and later refurbished in baroque style, contains precious winged altarpieces and historic religious frescoes. The opening of the scenic Mittelgebirgsbahn tramway in 1900 established Lans as a fashionable summer retreat for Innsbruck's urban elite, followed in the 20th century by international acclaim for the world-renowned Lanserhof health resort.

Getting There

Lans boasts rapid and scenic connectivity from nearby Innsbruck. Motorists departing the A13 Brenner Autobahn take the Innsbruck-Mitte or Patsch exits, following the L9 regional road straight onto the sunny plateau. A quintessential travel experience is riding the historic Mittelgebirgsbahn (Tram Line 6 of the IVB public transport company), a nostalgic forest tramway that winds from Innsbruck-Bergisel through dense pine woodlands up to Lans. In addition, frequent regional commuter buses operated by the VVT transit network run on tight schedules connecting Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof directly to Lans.

Tips

A summer afternoon at Lake Lans (Lanser See) is an essential highlight: naturally therapeutic moorland waters, expansive sunbathing lawns, paddleboat rentals, and lakeside dining deliver refreshing relaxation framed by panoramas of the Karwendel mountains. Walkers will delight in circling the protected Lanser Moor, a biodiverse peatland wetland dotted with water lilies and rare alpine flora. Golf enthusiasts can play the scenic 9-hole course of the Innsbruck-Igls Golf Club in Lans, while gourmands should dine at the historic Gasthof Wilder Mann, a multi-award-winning restaurant serving refined Tyrolean gastronomy. In winter, Mount Patscherkofel offers family skiing and winter walking.
